title: opportunistic-collective-coalescer-and-kernel-resynthesis-for-tp-hotpaths
author: Sofia Martinez
release_notes: Introduce opportunistic collective coalescer and a small-kernel resynthesis path that reduces per-collective overheads on TP workloads; measurable throughput and latency improvements for multi-GPU inference.
description:
Context / Motivation: Tensor-parallel inference workloads spend a non-trivial fraction of wall time in many small collectives (alltoall/allreduce) and short-lived kernel launches when sequence lengths and micro-batch packing vary. This PR adds an opportunistic collective coalescer that merges closely-timed small collectives into a consolidated launch when safe, plus a lightweight kernel resynthesis component that generates tuned microkernels for the hot small-sequence paths at runtime. The goal is to reduce NCCL/kernel launch overhead and improve overlap between comm and compute, without changing existing APIs or requiring offline compile steps.

What this PR changes (single-string summary): Implement runtime/collectives/coalescer that buffers and coalesces eligible collectives within a configurable window; add runtime/compiler/kernel_resynth which JITs small fused kernels specialized for common (seq_len, hidden) tuples; adjust scheduler to prefer compute-forward stream ordering and to annotate coalesced collectives for KV-cache-friendly ordering; add perf harness, unit/integration tests, and docs.

Key design points: - Opportunistic coalescing window is adaptive: starts at 100us and grows/shrinks based on observed inter-collective gaps and overall SLO headroom. - Safety: coalescer observes token-level dependency metadata; it will not merge collectives across operations that would change correctness (e.g., KV cache writes or model-ordered reductions). - Kernel resynthesis is bounded: compiled kernels are small, cached per-(device,seq_len,hidden) triplet, and evicted by LRU to avoid memory bloat. The resynth path falls back to precompiled kernels on memory pressure or when JIT fails. - Scheduler changes include a heuristic to launch compute-heavy projection kernels on the compute stream immediately and delay non-critical launches until NCCL progress is in flight, improving overlap.

Performance: Microbenchmark numbers (internal perf-lab, TP-8, A100s, sequence distribution from real prod traces): - End-to-end throughput up to +26% for chat-like workloads with many short sequences (median +18%). - P95 latency reduction on small prompts: ~12–18% depending on batching. - NCCL launch/latency tail reduced by ~30% as measured by collectives/s and avg latency per collective. - KV-cache hit path unchanged; some small improvement (~4%) due to reordered coalesced launches avoiding redundant KV buffer syncs.

Commits (high-level): - Implement coalescer: runtime/collectives/coalescer.cpp/.h, +tests/perf/bench_collective_coalescer.py - Add kernel resynth module: runtime/compiler/kernel_resynth.cpp/.h, +runtime/compiler/Makefile tweaks - Scheduler integration: serving/scheduler/stream_optimizer.cpp - Tests: tests/unit/collective_coalescer_test.cc, tests/integration/tp_end2end_coalesce.sh - Docs: docs/perf/collective_coalescer.md - CI: ci/perf-lab.yml additions + a small windows to disable resynth in GPU-less CI

Files changed (high-level): - runtime/collectives/coalescer.cpp/h - runtime/compiler/kernel_resynth.cpp/h - serving/scheduler/stream_optimizer.cpp - tests/unit/collective_coalescer_test.cc - tests/perf/bench_collective_coalescer.py - docs/perf/collective_coalescer.md - ci/perf-lab.yml

Compatibility and safety notes: - No API/ABI changes. - Coalescer disabled by default in release builds; opt-in via REDWOOD_COALESCE=1 or per-deployment config in console. - Kernel resynthesis requires a writable tempfs on device; when unavailable the path is a no-op and the runtime uses fallback kernels. - Added extensive unit tests to exercise correctness across heterogenous GPU topologies; we also ran a canary suite on Dedicated clusters (TP-2/TP-8) before merge.

Review conversation (abridged): 
- Ethan Zhao (reviewer): "Nice direction. Two correctness asks: 1) ensure we never reorder collectives that cross KV cache write boundaries; 2) add a deterministic seed for the coalescer's adaptive backoff so tests are stable."
- Sofia (author): "Addressed both: coalescer tags ops with KV write flags and we added COALESCE_TEST_SEED env var for deterministic behavior in tests. Updated tests accordingly."
- Priya Nair (reviewer): "Kernel resynth looks promising but we should bound JIT memory. Please add eviction metrics and a hard cap. Also add a guard that disables resynth on preemptible instances."
- Sofia: "Added eviction metrics (collective_resynth_evictions) and RESYNTH_MAX_CACHE_MB config. Also added a cheap instance-type check to disable on preemptible/spot instances in the resynth manager."
- Lucas Reinhardt (reviewer): "CI failed on first run due to flaky timing in bench harness. Reran perf CI and added a 2s stabilization sleep in bench harness to reduce flakiness. LGTM after CI pass."

CI summary: - Static checks: passed - Unit tests: passed (collective_coalescer_test, kernel_resynth unit) - Integration: perf-lab required two reruns; first run showed a transient timing flake in bench_collective_coalescer; second run green. - Merge gating: all checks green at merge time.

Post-merge notes and follow-ups: - Created follow-up ENG tasks to: 1) expose per-tenant coalescer tuning in Console (ENG-4902), 2) explore combining coalescer with adaptive batching heuristics (ENG-4916), 3) add TPU-simulated sanity checks (ENG-4920). - Performance dashboards added to Console: new metric group "collective_coalescer" (collectives_coalesced, avg_coalesce_window_us, resynth_invocations).

Why this is different from previous work: earlier PRs focused on static NCCL tuning, stream prioritization, or KV prefetch heuristics. This change introduces an adaptive, correctness-aware consolidation layer plus an on-host microkernel JIT that together attack the high-overhead case of many small collectives + short kernels. The approach is intentionally opportunistic (runtime opt-in) to reduce blast radius and provide a safe migration path.

Notes for on-call / SRE: - The coalescer can be disabled via REDWOOD_COALESCE=0. - Watch metrics: collective_coalescer.coalesced_rate, resynth_errors, resynth_evictions. - In the unlikely case of deadlock symptoms, set REDWOOD_COALESCE=0 and restart serving workers; safe fallback to precompiled kernels is automatic.

Merge: Squash and merge after final approvals.

End of PR description.
